cards.explanation: Whole-genome sequencing covers a much wider set of regions.
cards.text: Sequencing restricted to the protein-coding exons is called {{c1::exome sequencing}}.
cards.question: Sequencing restricted to the protein-coding exons is called {{c1::exome sequencing}}.

cards.explanation: Many differences from the reference sequence are compatible with health.
cards.text: Finding a variant in a patient does not by itself establish its {{c1::pathogenicity}}.
cards.question: Finding a variant in a patient does not by itself establish its {{c1::pathogenicity}}.

cards.explanation: Effects range from partial reduction to complete absence of activity.
cards.text: A variant that reduces the normal activity of a gene product causes {{c1::loss of function}}.
cards.question: A variant that reduces the normal activity of a gene product causes {{c1::loss of function}}.

cards.explanation: Inheritance gives a clue to mechanism, with important exceptions.
cards.text: A recessive pedigree can suggest loss of function because one intact allele may supply {{c1::sufficient gene product}}.
cards.question: A recessive pedigree can suggest loss of function because one intact allele may supply {{c1::sufficient gene product}}.

cards.explanation: Several distinct changes can disrupt the same essential function.
cards.text: Different variants in the same gene producing the same disorder illustrate {{c1::allelic heterogeneity}}.
cards.question: Different variants in the same gene producing the same disorder illustrate {{c1::allelic heterogeneity}}.

cards.explanation: This explains how loss of function can produce a dominant phenotype.
cards.text: Disease caused by one functional copy producing too little product is called {{c1::haploinsufficiency}}.
cards.question: Disease caused by one functional copy producing too little product is called {{c1::haploinsufficiency}}.

cards.explanation: The altered product actively disrupts function, for example within a protein complex.
cards.text: A mutant protein that interferes with its normal counterpart has a {{c1::dominant-negative}} effect.
cards.question: A mutant protein that interferes with its normal counterpart has a {{c1::dominant-negative}} effect.

cards.explanation: This can have a greater effect than simply making fewer normal chains.
cards.text: In severe osteogenesis imperfecta, an abnormal collagen chain can disrupt {{c1::assembly of the collagen molecule}}.
cards.question: In severe osteogenesis imperfecta, an abnormal collagen chain can disrupt {{c1::assembly of the collagen molecule}}.

cards.explanation: This is one mechanism through which a receptor variant can confer gain of function.
cards.text: A receptor that signals without its ligand is {{c1::constitutively active}}.
cards.question: A receptor that signals without its ligand is {{c1::constitutively active}}.

cards.explanation: Different alleles of the same gene can cause loss or gain of function.
cards.text: The functional effect must be assigned to the specific {{c1::variant}} even when the disease gene is known.
cards.question: The functional effect must be assigned to the specific {{c1::variant}} even when the disease gene is known.

cards.explanation: Their effects can depend on gene dosage and on which sequences the breakpoints disrupt.
cards.text: Large deletions, duplications and inversions are examples of {{c1::structural variation}}.
cards.question: Large deletions, duplications and inversions are examples of {{c1::structural variation}}.

cards.explanation: Absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion can all affect exposure.
cards.text: Genetic effects on what the body does to a drug concern {{c1::pharmacokinetics}}.
cards.question: Genetic effects on what the body does to a drug concern {{c1::pharmacokinetics}}.

cards.explanation: Two patients with similar drug exposure can still have different responses.
cards.text: Genetic effects on how a target responds to a drug concern {{c1::pharmacodynamics}}.
cards.question: Genetic effects on how a target responds to a drug concern {{c1::pharmacodynamics}}.

cards.explanation: The molecular cause of a disorder can guide treatment selection.
cards.text: Tailoring care to individual biological and clinical differences is called {{c1::precision medicine}}.
cards.question: Tailoring care to individual biological and clinical differences is called {{c1::precision medicine}}.
